title: Grateful Dead Live at Alfred College on 1970-05-01
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > Sonic Solutions > CDR

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard recording of a legendary early‑70 Alfred College show, highlighted by a blistering New Speedway Boogie and stellar acoustic/electric transitions.
ai_review.review: The SBD capture is frequently praised as crisp, crystal‑clear and even “the best live sound ever,” with only occasional comments that the mix could be a touch tighter. Musically the performance shines – two acoustic guitars open the set, Jerry’s lead on New Speedway Boogie is called “killer,” and Pigpen‑era songs like Cold Jordan, The Other One and Love Light get rave reactions. Listeners note a few minor letdowns (the NRPS excerpt and a missing Cold Rain & Snow), but overall the show is remembered as one of the great early‑70 Dead concerts.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews are 4–5 stars, praising both sound quality and performance; only a handful of low‑rating or off‑topic comments exist.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners repeatedly describe the audio as crisp, crystal clear and “best live sound ever.” A few note minor mix quirks (slight speed issues, occasional drop‑outs), but overall the SBD is considered top‑tier.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Starts with a dual‑acoustic opening (Bob, Jerry, plus a second acoustic likely David Nelson), moves into electric jams (Jerry’s lead on New Speedway Boogie) and builds to Pigpen‑centric material; the transition from acoustic to electric is highlighted as seamless and energizing.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for trading licks with Bob on New Speedway Boogie and delivering scorching electric leads throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted playing rhythm/acoustic guitar on Love Light and the early acoustic numbers; praised for solid accompaniment.
